work_order.understanding: Five findings: four from the review of PR #13 (now main at 6c423f4) and one from QA. Three of the four review findings are real and confirmed by reading and rendering the code. (1) The BUG-4 guard at tests/components/ui.test.tsx:307 is /max-w-\\[\\d/, which matches only a bracket followed by an ASCII digit. (2) The fixture at :294 renders <main /> inside a Shell that already renders <main id="main"> (src/components/shell.tsx:18). I confirmed both by rendering them rather than by reading: the Shell fixture produces container.querySelectorAll('main').length === 2 and 'main main'.length === 1, and swapping the child to <div /> gives exactly 1 and 0. (3) All three files this ticket touches lack a trailing newline: tail -c 1 returns 7d for top-bar.tsx, 7d for shell.tsx, 3b for ui.test.tsx. One correction to the review's premises, re-confirmed: finding 3 says the repo is otherwise consistent about trailing newlines. It is not — 44 tracked .ts/.tsx/.mjs/.json/.css files lack one, including package.json and eslint.config.mjs. Fixing the three this ticket touches is still right; the rest is a separate decision. Finding 4 (scope reconciliation) asks for no code change. The QA overflow finding is dispositioned as not reproducing, and I re-measured it myself rather than inheriting v2's numbers. Chromium runs headless on this runner, so I installed dependencies, ran npm run sdlc:serve against the real production build, signed up through the actual /sign-up form over CDP and measured at 360x640. Result: documentElement.scrollWidth is 360 against clientWidth 360 on both / and /settings; the name link measures 108.77px wide and 44px tall; the Sign out button's right edge lands at 344, inside the viewport; the span computes text-overflow: ellipsis. These match v2's figures exactly. I then attributed QA's number rather than assuming it stale: stripping min-w-0 from the nav in the live page moves scrollWidth to exactly 548 and the name link to 312.81px, reproducing QA's 548px overflow. QA drove a build whose nav lacked min-w-0; the chain that fixes it is present and working on main, so the finding needs no code change. On the reviewer's objection that QA cannot sign in: .sdlc/config.yml sets qa_auth.mode: none, but sign-up is an unauthenticated flow and I verified end to end that it sets an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax tabs_session cookie and redirects to /. The path is /sign-up, not /signup: the config's qa_auth.signup_url says "/signup" but src/app/sign-up/page.tsx is the only sign-up route, so the config value points at a 404. I cannot change that (reserved path), so this plan routes QA to /sign-up explicitly. The one thing this version changes from v2 is prose, and it is a correction the reviewer was right to demand: v2's AC-2 and its tests[] case asserted that max-w-[9rem] and max-w-[120px] were spellings the old guard newly caught. That is false. I ran both regexes over them: 9 is an ASCII digit, so /max-w-\\[\\d/ already matched both max-w-[9rem] and max-w-[120px] (old=true for each). The genuinely newly caught spellings are the ones whose value does not begin with a digit — max-w-[--cap], max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)], max-w-[var(--x)] and max-w-[theme(cap)] (old=false, new=true for each). The code change is right and strictly wider; only the demonstration was wrong, and AC-2 instructs QA to falsify the premise explicitly, so an adversarial check would have failed a PR whose code was correct. I also checked the widened guard's own boundary, which the review did not: Tailwind 4's CSS-variable shorthand max-w-(--cap) carries no bracket and is still not matched by /max-w-\[/ (old=false, new=false). That is a disclosed limit, not a reason to widen again, and it is now stated in residual_risks rather than implied away.
work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes and one non-cause. (1) The BUG-4 guard encodes a ceiling syntax rather than the concept: /max-w-\\[\\d/ means 'a bracketed max-width whose value starts with an ASCII digit', but the intent is 'no max-width ceiling on the display name'. Every bracket-valued Tailwind max-width carries a bracket, so the digit is an unnecessary narrowing. What it genuinely let through were values not beginning with a digit — max-w-[--cap], max-w-[calc(...)], max-w-[var(...)] — not the digit-valued spellings such as max-w-[9rem] and max-w-[120px], which it always caught. (2) The fixture passes an element as Shell's children that duplicates one Shell already renders, so it asserts a DOM shape the application cannot produce — and React logs no validateDOMNesting warning for main-in-main, so it fails silently. (3) The three files were written without a final newline and nothing in the toolchain enforces one. NOT a cause: the QA 360px overflow. min-w-0 on the nav is present on main and load-bearing — removing it alone reproduces QA's 548px exactly. The build QA measured predates that class.
work_order.approach: Three small edits, all in files this ticket already rewrites, and no layout change. In tests/components/ui.test.tsx: widen the BUG-4 guard from /max-w-\\[\d/ to /max-w-\\[/ so any bracketed ceiling is caught, and amend the comment above it which currently claims to be 'the permanent guard against one coming back'. Replace the fixture's <main /> with <div />. Add one assertion that the name link itself does not carry shrink-0 — that is the class whose accidental addition reproduces QA's overflow while every existing assertion stays green. Append a trailing newline to the three files. Deliberately NOT changing top-bar.tsx's classes: the shrink chain measures correct at 360x640 and at the schema's maximum name length, so a layout edit would change working code on the strength of a finding that no longer holds. The only substantive difference from the rejected v2 is that AC-2's demonstration and the matching tests[] case now name spellings the old regex genuinely missed, and say so accurately.

If QA sees 548, the fix is to find which build lacks the class, not to change the layout.

work_order.debate_summary: v3 changes exactly what the review of v2 required, and I verified that requirement rather than accepting it. The single objection held: v2's AC-2 claimed the old guard missed max-w-[9rem] and max-w-[120px], and instructed QA to falsify that premise. Running both regexes shows 9 is an ASCII digit, so the old guard matched both — the criterion asserted something untrue about its own subject, and an adversarial QA following its own instructions would have failed a correct PR. The code change was right and stays; the prose is corrected to name spellings the old guard genuinely missed (max-w-[--cap], max-w-[calc(...)], max-w-[var(...)], all old=false new=true), and the claim that [9rem] or [120px] were previously missed is dropped. While checking the widened guard I found a boundary the review did not examine — Tailwind 4's unbracketed max-w-(--cap) is still unmatched — which is disclosed in residual_risks rather than fixed, since the review's sanction covered /max-w-\[/ and no more. Nothing else in v2 changed. I re-derived v2's load-bearing measurements from scratch rather than inheriting them: the layout numbers reproduce exactly on a production build, and both review findings now rest on rendered DOM rather than on reading. Baseline re-confirmed green at 7 files and 86 tests, after npm ci (an uninstalled checkout fails typecheck, which is an environment artifact worth knowing). No route_request: the route was adequate, and the correction the objection demanded belonged to planning.
residual_risks: The widened guard still does not catch Tailwind 4's unbracketed CSS-variable shorthand max-w-(--cap) — verified old=false new=false — because /max-w-\[/ requires a bracket. A ceiling written that way would reintroduce BUG-4 uncaught. Closing it needs a second alternative such as /max-w-[-[(]/, which exceeds what the review sanctioned, so it is disclosed here and left to a maintainer.

The widened guard catches a bracketed Tailwind max-width only, not an inline style={{maxWidth:'120px'}} or a CSS rule in globals.css. A disclosed limit carried forward from the review; AC-1 decides the behaviour.

AC-1 cannot be satisfied by CI. jsdom computes no layout, so if QA does not run it in a browser the overflow is neither confirmed fixed nor confirmed open. This plan reduces that risk rather than removing it: AC-1 is a regression guard over a state QA can reach unauthenticated, and the attribution numbers are in how_to_verify so QA can tell a regression from a different build at a glance.

Every signed-in check in this ticket depends on QA completing the /sign-up form, because qa_auth.mode is none and no credentials are provisioned. If that flow breaks, AC-1 is unreachable for a reason unrelated to this change.

review.detail:
The new comment at tests/components/ui.test.tsx:337 attributes QA's 548px overflow to shrink-0 on the name link, but that class produces 579px. The 548 figure comes from removing min-w-0 from the nav — a different element and a different class. The assertion itself is sound and does bite; only the stated attribution is wrong.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:337`

Evidence: Two independent headless-Chromium sessions against `TABS_ENV=local next build && next start`, signed in through the real /sign-up form at 360x640, reproducing identically. Adding shrink-0 to the name link only (a[href="/settings"]): {"scrollW":579,"clientW":345,"nameW":344.09,"signoutRight":579.33}. Removing min-w-0 from the nav instead: {"scrollW":548,"clientW":345,"nameW":312.81,"signoutRight":548.05}. 548 is reproduced exactly by the min-w-0 removal, which is what the work order's own evidence and root_cause attribute it to ('removing min-w-0 from the nav moves scrollWidth to exactly 548'). The comment at lines 337-339 says shrink-0 on the name link 'is the class whose accidental addition reproduces the 548px horizontal overflow QA measured'. Confirmed the guard bites: injecting shrink-0 makes the suite fail at ui.test.tsx:340, so nothing is left unguarded — but a future maintainer reproducing the comment gets 579 and may conclude the guard or measurement is broken.

Fix: Reword the comment to state what was measured: shrink-0 on the name link reproduces a horizontal overflow of the same shape but a different magnitude (579px), and it is the min-w-0 removal that reproduces QA's 548px exactly. Either attribution keeps the assertion; the comment should name both numbers rather than one.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:315`

Evidence: Built globals.css through @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.3 from the repo root, PR and main test file, with work-order.json and review/ moved out first (both are scanned and quote the same tokens, which masks the result entirely). review.title: The new comment asserts 'Every arbitrary-value Tailwind max-width carries that bracket.' Tailwind 4.3.3 also accepts the unbracketed CSS-variable shorthand max-w-(--cap), which it compiles to a real rule, so the claim justifying the guard's completeness is false for the pinned version. A ceiling written that way reintroduces BUG-4 uncaught. The work order discloses this in residual_risks; the disclosure never reached the comment.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:313`

Evidence: Both regexes over every spelling named: max-w-[9rem] old=true new=true; max-w-[120px] old=true new=true; max-w-[--cap], [calc(100%-2rem)], [var(--x)], [theme(cap)] old=false new=true; max-w-(--cap) old=false new=false. Dropping the lone string 'max-w-(--cap)' into the repo root produced .max-w-\(--cap\) { max-width: var(--cap) } in a fresh build, so the gap is real and not theoretical. Scale utilities (max-w-xs, max-w-3xl) are also uncaught, which is correct.

Fix: Soften to 'Every bracketed arbitrary-value max-width carries that bracket', and either widen to /max-w-[-[(]/ or note in the comment that Tailwind 4's unbracketed shorthand is deliberately outside the net. The work order judged widening to exceed the review's sanction; recording the limit is cheaper.

validated_work_order.approach: Draw the source boundary Tailwind was never given, in the one place the build config lives: add `@source not '../../tests';` to src/app/globals.css immediately after the `@import 'tailwindcss'` line. Nothing else in product code changes — no component, no class list, no layout, no test assertion weakened. This is deliberately not a rewording of the comment. The comment is accurate and its naming is load-bearing for AC-2, which asks QA to falsify the guard's premise by checking that max-w-[9rem] and max-w-[120px] were already caught and only the non-digit spellings are new; a comment stripped of its spellings would leave that criterion unverifiable and would put the bug back the moment the next person documents a guard. The exclusion also removes the pre-existing dead .max-w-[120px] rule, so the shipped stylesheet ends up with exactly the two max-w rules the app actually uses. Add tests/lib/tailwind-source-scope.test.ts as the regression guard: it asserts the exclusion exists and names tests/, that it is not source(none), that tests/ still contains class tokens src/ does not (so the guard cannot pass vacuously once the comment is reworded someday), and that the path resolves to tests/ and to nothing under src/. That last assertion is the one that matters for safety — an over-broad exclusion would strip styling the app renders with, and nothing else in this repo would catch it, because the class names still appear in src/. I verified the exclusion by building both revisions and diffing the complete emitted rule set rather than trusting the reasoning: the fix drops 3 dead max-w rules plus .uppercase and .focus:absolute, all five confirmed dead by grepping src/, and retains every rule the app uses.
assumptions: Tailwind 4.3's `@source not` is honoured by @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.3 as pinned in package.json, and by next build through PostCSS — confirmed by building, not by documentation.

docs/ui.md, docs/prd.md and docs/trd.md are not contributing class spellings that the app depends on. They are outside src/ but were inside main's scan; the fix removes them from it. The full rule-set diff is the check on this, and it showed only dead rules lost.

No component composes class names dynamically from values that never appear literally in src/ — checked src/components/ui/{button,money,card,skeleton,input,empty-state}.tsx and every variant/size/colour map is a literal string in the same file, so the scan still sees them.

QA's reported layout measurements (scrollWidth 360 == clientWidth 360, name link 108.77x44, sign-out right edge 344) are sound and need no re-derivation; I reproduced AC-1's build-side state and QA reproduced the browser-side numbers to the decimal across all five criteria.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every load-bearing claim here is something I ran rather than inherited. I reproduced QA's delta from scratch: main emits 3 max-w rules, the PR head emits 5, the two new ones being calc(100%-2rem) and var(--x) — an exact match to the report, which is why I trust its measurements. I then built the fix and diffed the complete emitted rule set instead of reasoning about it, because an exclusion that is too broad would strip styling the app depends on and no unit test would notice; that diff is what caused me to reject source(none) after seeing it drop 20 used rules. The five rules the fix removes are each confirmed dead by grepping src/ — .uppercase and .focus:absolute appear only in test comments, and neither max-w-[120px], max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] nor max-w-[var(--x)] matches any element. The retained rules were checked positively, not assumed. The new guard was verified to fail with the fix reverted and to fail against the source(none) variant it exists to reject, so it is a real assertion rather than a restatement of the fix; I also rewrote one case after finding it failed degenerately rather than for its own reason. The full gate is green at 8 files and 90 tests and the production server boots and serves. What holds me below the mid-90s is the same class of gap as before and it is environmental, not analytical: I cannot inspect the exact preview QA drove, and the pre-existing max-w-[120px] rule shows this mechanism predates the ticket, so a scan root I have not found could still exist. AC-6 is written to catch a rule appearing in the shipped stylesheet on every future run precisely because that residual cannot be closed here.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: The plan under trial diagnosed the mechanism correctly and then chose the single remedy that cannot work, so it had to disclose the defect instead of fixing it — and QA failed it on introduced_by_pr. The contestable judgement was treating a build-configuration gap as a prose problem. Once the exclusion is added, the comment can keep naming the spellings that make AC-2 falsifiable, the pre-existing dead rule disappears too, and the bug cannot return without someone adding a new scan root.

risks: The exclusion is a path relative to src/app/globals.css. If that file ever moves, '../../tests' silently resolves elsewhere and the exclusion does nothing — this is why the guard asserts the path resolves to tests/ exactly rather than merely containing the string 'tests'.

Tailwind's auto-detection also reads other roots. If a future root (e.g. a Storybook directory or a scripts/ fixture) starts naming class spellings, it will reintroduce dead rules the same way; the non-vacuity case in the new guard is the tripwire for tests/, not a general one.

Globals.css is Tailwind's entry, so a mistake here breaks all styling at once rather than one component. That is why the full rule-set diff in the QA script matters more than the targeted grep, and why the guard forbids source(none).

QA's previous run drove commit e709a0e; this attempt changes globals.css, so the built asset hash changes. Nothing should depend on that hash, but the run should confirm the app still boots and renders rather than comparing screenshots across builds.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Tailwind 4's automatic source detection scans the whole project, so tests/ is a production stylesheet input on the same footing as src/. Every class-shaped token in a test file — including tokens inside an explanatory comment — is compiled into a utility and emitted. PR #18 widened the BUG-4 guard from /max-w-\\[\d/ to /max-w-\\[/, and the comment explaining the widening necessarily names the spellings the old guard missed (max-w-[--cap], max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)], max-w-[var(--x)]); two of those are valid arbitrary values, so Tailwind emitted .max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] and .max-w-[var(--x)] into the stylesheet every user downloads. Neither matches any element, so both are inert. The same mechanism already accounted for the pre-existing dead .max-w-[120px] rule on main, which comes from the same comment. The defect is in the build configuration, not the prose: src/app/globals.css declares no source boundary, so nothing stops a test-only class-shaped token from reaching shipped CSS. v1 diagnosed the mechanism correctly but chose the one remedy that cannot work, because the comment must keep naming the spellings in order for AC-2's demonstration to mean anything.

cases: BUG-1 reproduction: with the `@source not '../../tests'` line absent, the guard fails naming the missing directive — this is the state PR #18 shipped, where tests/components/ui.test.tsx's comment made two dead max-w rules reach the production stylesheet
the exclusion is not source(none): applying the source(none) plus explicit @source variant fails this case, which is how the variant that drops 20 used rules is kept out
non-vacuity: tests/ still names class spellings src/ does not use, so removing tests/ from the scan is observable rather than a no-op
the exclusion resolves to tests/ and to nothing under src/ or at the project root, so it cannot be widened into stripping styling the app renders with

validated_work_order.understanding: The previous plan was not wrong about the code — every one of its five acceptance criteria passed, and I confirmed QA's numbers are reproducible. But its diagnosis of BUG-1 was wrong in a way that made the fix impossible, and that is why QA failed. v1 correctly identified the MECHANISM: Tailwind scans source for class-name-like tokens, so a class spelling named in a comment becomes a real utility candidate. It then made the remedy 're-word the comment', and explicitly put rewording out of scope while disclosing the consequence. That is a plan that cannot converge: the comment has to name the spellings the widened guard now catches, because naming them is the whole demonstration AC-2 asks QA to falsify. Any fix that keeps the naming and removes the emitted rules has to change something other than the prose — and v1 never identified what that was. So it accepted, by disclosure, a defect it had every means to fix, and QA returned fail on introduced_by_pr. I reproduced the delta myself rather than inheriting it: built origin/main (cc09d67) and the PR head (e709a0e) with the same toolchain and node_modules, and grepped the emitted CSS. Main ships 3 max-w rules, the PR ships 5; the two new ones are .max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] and .max-w-[var(--x)], matching QA's report exactly. The premise is one layer deeper than v1 stated, and this is the part that matters: the scan reads the whole project, not just the file a class belongs to. tests/components/ui.test.tsx is a Tailwind source, so its comments are production input. That also explains the pre-existing max-w-[120px] dead rule v1 treated as background — it comes from the same test comment, so main was already shipping one and this PR shipped three. I tested the fix by building it, not by reasoning about it. Adding `@source not '../../tests';` to src/app/globals.css drops the emitted set to the two live rules (max-w-[360px] on the sign-in/sign-up card and settings form, max-w-[720px] on Shell's main) and also removes the pre-existing max-w-[120px]. I diffed the FULL rule set, not just max-w, because an exclusion that is too broad would silently strip styling the app depends on and no unit test would notice. Only two further rules disappear, .uppercase and .focus:absolute, and I grepped src/ for both: neither is used by any component, so both were dead. Everything the app uses survives — truncate, min-w-0, shrink-0, max-w-[360px], max-w-[720px] all still emitted. I also built and rejected the more obvious source(none) variant with an explicit @source '../../src', because it drops 20 rules the app does reference (container, hidden, relative, filter, ring, transition and more); it would have been a silent styling regression traded for a cosmetic one. The new guard is at the level the bug lives — the exclusion, not the comment's wording — because rewording only relocates the problem to whoever names a class in a test comment next. I verified it bites: with the fix reverted it fails, and the source(none) variant fails the guard written against it. Full gate green at 8 files and 90 tests, and the production server boots and serves /sign-up with the live card rule present.
unknowns: Whether some scan root outside src/ and tests/ contributes spellings the app depends on. docs/*.md were inside main's scan and are outside it now; the full rule-set diff found nothing live among the losses, but a root contributing a rule that a component already gets from src/ would be invisible to that comparison.

Whether Vercel's build environment resolves `@source not '../../tests'` the same way the local production build did. The path is relative to the CSS file and both builds share the toolchain, so this should hold, but it is not verified on Vercel.

Why .uppercase and .focus:absolute are emitted at all — they come from tests/ but from a different file (tests/integration/auth.test.ts and the skip-link comment) than BUG-1's. The fix removes them as a side effect; QA should confirm the app does not rely on either, which the full rule-set diff already indicates but which no browser check covers directly.
